source.title: Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models
source.authors: Bryce Grant; Xijia Zhao; Peng Wang

page_placements.theme: Reconstruction metrics do not determine functional preservation

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE reconstructions preserve model behavior using rollout success, a different measure from linear predictability or error scaling. The tested results bear on V5, not the central dark-matter error claims.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates task success when SAE reconstructions replace activations, including comparisons across pooling methods and architectures. It does not measure SAE error vectors, linear predictability from input activations, error-norm scaling, overlap of failed tokens across SAE sizes, or loss effects compared with random errors. SAE feature ablation and steering results are not results about reconstruction error and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (robot VLA policies), the study replaces activations with SAE reconstructions, which drops the SAE error, and measures task rollout success. It also shows that keeping the error (residual write-back) removes the mean-pool collapse. These results bear on V5: whether behaviour is lost unless the error term is kept. It does not measure error-vector structure, scaling or random-error controls, so V1–V4 and V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that pooling preference depends on the signal kept as well as the architecture (language-pathway steering needs per-token SAEs). Also add that the mean-pool collapse holds only under replacement write-back and disappears with residual write-back on OFT, GR00T and X-VLA. The authors avoid temporal-contrastive SAEs and do not frame results as SAE error or dark matter.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs and tests activation reconstruction through VLA task rollouts; it does not measure linear SAE-error prediction, error norms, or dark-matter scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Pooling choice and architecture change rollout fidelity. The paper also reports that mean-pool replacement write-back collapses success on some models, while residual write-back avoids that collapse on OFT, GR00T, and X-VLA.

fits_no_version.finding: π0.5 mean-pool SAEs reach normalized MSE ≤0.05 (R2>0.95), yet success falls 89.9%→3.3%. Base OpenVLA SAEs with R2 0.87–0.96 give 0% success. Small reconstruction error, outsized behavioural harm, but there is no matched random-error control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity (R2/MSE) does not predict behavioural preservation in closed-loop policies.

record.problems: For the V5 evidence, the reported SAE rollout tables do not give uncertainty estimates. The study concerns VLA task success and reconstruction pooling, not a direct analysis of SAE error structure. The authors note the temporal-SAE contrastive coefficient was not swept and that results depend on write-back choice.
record.rows_left_out: Additional pooling results are reported in §3.4, App. H.1-H.2, and Tables 24 and 9, including layer-level plots, sparsity k sweeps, and isolated residual-write-back comparisons. These are omitted to keep the record focused on the principal aggregate and per-suite reconstruction evaluations; they do not test V1-V4 or V6.

untested.parts: No linear prediction of the SAE error from input activations.
No per-token error-norm prediction, no overlap of failure contexts across SAE sizes. The k sweep reports rollout success, not error norms.
No comparison with random errors of matched norm; the random-direction controls are for activation injection, not SAE error.
No split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
Circuit analyses are not tested. Steering through SAE reconstructions (Tab. 9) is reported but not captured in rows.
No end-to-end SAE training and no architecture comparison aimed at shrinking the error. Pooling, temporal loss and k are varied, but only rollout success is measured.

missing.what: Base OpenVLA (discrete tokens): hooking SAEs (R2 0.87–0.96) gives 0% task success on all but the final layer.

record.verdict_notes: Two items in rows_left_out are declared omitted but bear directly on V5 and should be added as rows. (1) Residual vs replacement write-back (App. M): mean-pool OFT 0→73.3%, GR00T 2→82%, X-VLA 3.3→100%. This is the clearest 'keep the error' test. (2) Tab. 24 k sweep: per-token success at k=32 is 26.7–63.3%, near baseline at k=128. The record's claim that these omissions do not bear on any version is wrong. Tab. 9 (steering through SAE reconstructions: X-VLA 54 vs 50 raw, GR00T L2 66 vs 94 raw) bears on V5's steering part. Mean-pool and temporal rows mix loss from dropping the error with loss from pooling or the contrastive loss; per-token rows are the cleanest V5 test. Tranche changed to T3: new setting (VLAs, rollout success). No uncertainty is given for Tables 11, 12 and 17.

versions.untested_parts: No measurement of the SAE error vector’s linear predictability from input activations.
No per-token error-norm scaling or comparison of which contexts fail across SAE sizes.
Does not compare model loss after SAE reconstruction replacement with random errors of the same size.
Does not separate linear and nonlinear SAE error components or test further dictionary learning on them.
Tests task success under SAE reconstruction replacement, not the effect of SAE error on circuit analyses or steering analyses generally.
Compares pooling and write-back choices, but does not establish whether dark matter mostly arises from SAE training or whether it shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: Per-token SAE replacement on X-VLA, OFT and π0.5 (goal, object, libero_10 suites)
relationships.reason: Dropping the SAE error cuts rollout success meaningfully: X-VLA 95.2→50.6, OFT 95.4→80.1, π0.5 libero_10 86.0→70.3 (r04, r10, r16, r22, r25, r28, r31, r34, r37).
relationships.display_finding: Removing the error reduced rollout success from 95.2 to 50.6 for X-VLA, 95.4 to 80.1 for OFT, and 86.0 to 70.3 for π0.5 on libero_10.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Per-token SAE replacement on X-VLA, OFT and π0.5 (goal, object, libero_10 suites)
source_check.reason: Tables 11, 12 and 17 show meaningful success losses after reconstruction-only replacement in these settings; correcting the four OFT per-suite baselines preserves this conclusion.

relationships.condition: Temporal-contrastive and mean-pooled SAEs under replacement write-back on π0.5, OFT and X-VLA (temporal)
relationships.reason: Success collapses (π0.5 mean-pool 89.9→3.3, OFT 95.4→7.3) or drops sharply under temporal SAEs. Per the text, residual write-back, which keeps the error, restores mean-pool success on OFT, GR00T and X-VLA.
relationships.display_finding: Mean-pooled replacement reduced success from 89.9 to 3.3 for π0.5 and 95.4 to 7.3 for OFT, while temporal replacements also caused sharp losses; retaining the error restored mean-pooled success on OFT, GR00T, and X-VLA.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Temporal-contrastive and mean-pooled SAEs under replacement write-back on π0.5, OFT and X-VLA (temporal)
source_check.reason: Tables 11 and 12 show reduced success under temporal reconstruction and severe mean-pool replacement losses on π0.5 and OFT. Section 4.6 and Appendix M report rescue with residual write-back on OFT, GR00T and X-VLA.

relationships.condition: Per-token SAE on GR00T DiT and π0.5 libero_spatial; X-VLA mean-pool; GR00T temporal
relationships.reason: Losses are small (GR00T 83.9→80.0, π0.5 spatial 92.8→90.0), so the loss depends on architecture and pooling. Per Tab. 24 (not rowed), it also depends on k.
relationships.display_finding: Success fell only from 83.9 to 80.0 for GR00T and 92.8 to 90.0 for π0.5 spatial, with losses varying by architecture, pooling, and k.

relation.reason: The study directly measures task success after replacing activations with SAE reconstructions and compares pooling and write-back conditions.

tranche.reason: Reconstruction-only rollout evaluations test functional preservation in the new setting of robot VLA policies, bearing on V5.

source_check.notes: Appendix M reports residual write-back rescue at single matched cells on OFT, GR00T and X-VLA; no π0.5 residual-write-back result is reported. Random-direction injection controls do not constitute a matched random SAE-error control for V3.

statements.correction: Table 12: OFT per-token success 95.4%→80.1%, without reported intervals. Table 24: π0.5 reconstruction comparisons across sparsity settings, n=30 per cell; caption reports disjoint Wilson 95% intervals between per-token and mean-pool arms.
statements.problem: The OFT result and recipe match, but the general statement that reconstruction rollout tables lack uncertainty overlooks the supplementary sparsity comparison.
